svg.title: crux Pratt certificate and flag decryption
svg.desc: Root 256-bit prime has eight child certificates: five copies of 2, 1777, 117013415621 and a 62-digit prime. The root witness is 3. The encoded certificate is 3891 bytes; first AES-CBC ciphertext is 3904 bytes and base64 input 5208 characters. The checker decrypts and verifies the certificate, then uses SHA-256 of its unpadded bytes as the second AES key. Decrypting the 64-byte flag ciphertext with that key and the same IV, then removing padding, yields the flag.
svg.text: crux - the proof tree and the flag decrypt
Each factor gets its own certificate, including all five copies of 2.
32 little-endian target bytes · witness a = 3 · root has 8 child certificates
62 digits; full value in the table
Children multiply (with multiplicities) to p − 1; each child proves its own primality.
3891 proof bytes → AES-256-CBC + PKCS#7 → 3904 ciphertext bytes → 5208 Base64 characters
Pratt test: a^(p−1) ≡ 1 (mod p); for each distinct q | p−1, a^((p−1)/q) ≠ 1 (mod p).
Checker: Base64 decode → first AES-CBC decrypt → remove padding → certificate plaintext
Parse and verify the tree against the target prime; SHA-256(plaintext) supplies the second AES key.
64-byte flag ciphertext → AES-256-CBC decrypt (same IV) → remove padding → flag
